critical_evidence.evidence: CARFAX shows dated oil changes in 09/2020, 06/2021, 03/2022 and 02/2024, then nothing until the dealer PDI in 09/2026. That leaves about 2 years 7 months and about 7,800 mi with no reported service. There is no reported brake-fluid flush in six years. Absence of an entry is not proof it was not done, but nothing documents it.

This is a 2020 ND2 built well after Mazda revised the 6MT internals. The early-ND1 (2016/early-2017) gearbox build-date concern does not apply. CARFAX shows no reported transmission work. A warm-gearbox test drive is still part of the PPI.

The RF has targa-seal and roof drains rather than soft-top drains, so water ingress still applies. The interior photos show floor mats in place, debris on the carpet and sill area, and no lifted carpet. No photos of the drain areas.

CARFAX reports an open recall: NHTSA 24V-695 / Mazda 6924I, an air bag/SAS control module software update, issued 09/18/2024 with remedy available. It was not shown completed, even though the dealer PDI was done on 09/28/2026.
The listing makes no new-tire or new-battery claim. The photos show Bridgestone tires with no legible DOT date. No tire or battery receipts appear in CARFAX.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are present: VIN, decode, clean guaranteed title, a 2-owner CARFAX with dated oil changes, and a fees-included price. The maintenance half is incomplete. There are no invoices, no brake-fluid or driveline-fluid entries, a 2.5-year reporting gap, and no photos of the underside, drains or tire dates.

condition.rationale: No mechanical fault is stated, but the photos show neglect-level presentation. The nose and grille are bug-caked and the front lip looks scuffed. The floor mats and sills are dirty with debris, there is a stain and wear on the passenger cushion, and the leather shift knob is worn. Rear rotors show surface rust. Nothing proves good mechanical condition, and the underside of an Ohio/Michigan car is unexamined.

price_value.rationale: At $25,596, the price is about 12% above the $22,862 fair-value midpoint and above the $24,012 top of the band. That is offset only partly by fees being included. Comparable RF Clubs sold at $22,000 (2019, 32.6k mi) and $24,750 (2021, 31.5k mi).

mission_fit.rationale: This is a manual, reliable, easily resold ND2 roadster that fits the enthusiast-bridge brief. However, the asking price sits well above the $10,000-$19,000 ideal band, though under the $27,000 ceiling.

logistics.rationale: Cleveland, TN is a long fly-and-drive from Carmel. It is a dealer, so an independent PPI is plausible but not stated. CA registration and smog should be straightforward for a stock 2020.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits combine here: an ND2 181 hp/7,500 rpm engine, Club trim (LSD, Bilstein), a 6MT and an RF hardtop, in an attractive gray. Brembo/BBS fitment is not established.

what_would_change_verdict: A clean independent PPI with dry, minimally corroded underside, healthy gearbox/clutch and roof function would lift condition substantially.
A price movement toward the $22,000-$24,000 fair-value band, or the dealer closing the recall and supplying fresh fluids/tires, would improve value.
Receipts filling the 2024-2026 service gap and showing a brake-fluid flush would raise documentation.
Significant underside rust, gearbox grinding, RF roof faults or water ingress found at PPI would move it down sharply.
evidence.mission_note: A manual ND2 RF Club is a strong match for the enthusiast-bridge brief and should be easy to resell in 6-24 months. Its asking price, however, sits above the ideal band and above fair value, so the fit is on spec rather than on price.
evidence.rationale: The VIN, decode and CARFAX establish a 2020 ND2 MX-5 RF Club with a 6-speed manual, a guaranteed clean title, 2 personal owners and an odometer of 36,986-36,987 consistent across the photo and report. The CARFAX documents four dated oil changes through 02/2024 at 29,208 mi, then no reported service until a dealer PDI in 09/2026. It shows no reported brake-fluid or driveline-fluid work at any point. It also shows an open airbag-module software recall (24V-695) that remains unclosed after the dealer's own PDI. The photos show a car not reconditioned for sale: a bug-caked nose and scuffed front lip, debris-strewn carpets, a stained passenger cushion and a worn shift knob. No visible modifications or warning lights appear in the views examined. Six years of Ohio and Michigan ownership leaves underside corrosion, tire age, RF roof function and cabin water ingress unexamined. At $25,596 fees included, the asking price is roughly 12% above the $22,862 mileage-adjusted fair-value midpoint.
evidence.next_action: Ask CarsNow for the itemised out-the-door price, written PPI permission, tire DOT and underside photos, and the Precision Masters PDI work order, and request that recall 24V-695 be closed at a Mazda dealer before any deposit.
